scope: Diagnosis and cytokine-targeted treatment of adult-onset Still's disease, as described in this 2018 review.

keyRecommendations.text: The Yamaguchi criteria are the most widely used, but they include exclusion of infection, malignancy, and other rheumatic disease and should follow a broad work-up.
The typical rash is salmon pink, macular or maculopapular, transient, and mainly visible during fever spikes on the proximal limbs or trunk.

Pathogenesis centres on innate-cell activation and overproduction of IL-1, IL-6, and IL-18. The review states that two IL-1 antagonists have been approved, and describes anakinra as a recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist with benefit in case series and uncontrolled studies.

clinicalBottomLine: Suspect AoSD from spiking high fever and a transient salmon-pink rash, apply Yamaguchi criteria only after exclusions, and treat the IL-1-centred inflammatory drive, with anakinra the first biologic described as beneficial in uncontrolled series.
notableCaveats: A glycosylated-ferritin percentage threshold is not stated in the prose used here, so it is not asked. The review's abstract says two IL-1 antagonists are approved, while a later sentence discusses anakinra and canakinumab trial phases; questions use the approval sentence and the description of anakinra separately.
